questions.question: Which of the following statements is** not **correct with respect to the Parliament of India?

options.text: The President summons each house of the Parliament to meet.
The President declares the House adjourned sine die.
Prorogation of the house is done by President.
Prorogation terminates a session of the House.

questions.solution:
__Option 2 is not correct.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Parliament shall meet at **least twice a year**. The **maximum gap** between **two sessions of the Parliament cannot be more than six months**.
 
• The** President** from time to time **summons each house of the Parliament to meet.**
 
• There are usually **three sessions** in a year :
 
 
• Budget session
 
• Monsoon session
 
• Winter session
 
 
 
• A sitting of a parliament can be **terminated by adjournment or adjournment sine die or prorogation or dissolution.**
 
• **Adjournment**: It suspends the work in a sitting **for a specified time**, which may be hours, days, and weeks.
 
• **Adjournment sine die**: It means terminating a sitting of Parliament** for an indefinite period.**
 
 
• The power of adjournment sine die lies with the **presiding officer of the House** and not the president. **Hence, Option 2 is correct answer of this question.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Prorogation**: After the presiding officer declares the House adjourned sine die, within the next few days, the **President issues a notification** for the prorogation of the session.

 
 
• However, the President can also prorogue the house while in session.
 
 
 
• **Dissolution**: It **ends the very life of the existing house** and a new house is constituted after general elections are held.
 
 
• **Rajya Sabha** being a permanent house is** not subject to dissolution,** while** Lok Sabha is subject to dissolution**.

questions.question: What is the area of the remaining portion of a circle of radius 14 cm when a square with maximum possible area inscribed in it is removed from it? (Use pi = (22)/(7) )
questions.solution:
**Concept:**

For a square to be inscribed in a circle, its diagonal is equal to the diameter of the circle.

Let the side of the square be a 

Diagonal = a × √2

**Solution:**

Since the diagonal of the square equals the diameter of the circle,

a × √2 = 2 × radius = 2 × 14 = 28 cm

a = 28 ÷ √2 = 14√2 cm

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/65e6d9e1a087cbfa80c02f18df62ee4177cb4584f691c06e3cbb2e8e90bf2c49.png] 

The area of the square is:

Aₛ = a² = (14√2)² = 196 × 2 = 392 cm² 

The area of the circle is,

A꜀ = π × r² = (22 ÷ 7) × 14² = (22 ÷ 7) × 196 = 616 cm².

Remaining area = A꜀ - Aₛ = 616 - 392 = **224 cm²**.

• However, the battle was a bloody and chaotic affair, and **Rajaditya was killed in the fighting. **

• The Battle of Takkolam had a significant impact on the political landscape of southern India.

questions.question: What does the acronym 'GIF' stand for?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Graphics Interchange Format**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Graphics Interchange Format (GIF)** is a bitmap image format that was developed by CompuServe in 1987.
 
• GIFs are widely used on the internet due to their wide support and portability between applications and operating systems.
 
• They support up to 8 bits per pixel, allowing a single image to reference a palette of up to 256 distinct colors chosen from the 24-bit RGB color space.
 
• GIFs can be used for small animations and low-resolution film clips due to their support for animation and transparency.
 
• The format's use of lossless compression means that the image quality is not degraded through the compression process.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• GIF became popular because it was one of the first two image formats commonly used on the web, the other being the JPEG format.
 
• It is particularly well-suited for images with large areas of solid color.
 
• GIFs use the Lempel–Ziv–Welch (LZW) lossless data compression technique to reduce the file size without degrading the visual quality.
 
• Despite the limited color palette, GIFs are a popular format for memes and short animations on social media platforms.
 
• In 2012, the Oxford American Dictionary named "GIF" as the word of the year.

questions.question: N women can complete the project in 12 days. If 5 women are less employed then it will take 15 more days to complete the same project, then find the number of women initially employed.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

N women can complete the project in T days. 

If M women are less employed then it will take d more days to complete the same project, 

Then the number of women initially employed = N = (M times (T + d))/(d)

According to the question, 

The initial number of women = N

The time is taken by N women to complete the task,T = 12 days

The number of women removed from the project, M = 5

The additional number of days required, d = 15 days

Now,

⇒ N = (5 times (12 + 15))/(15) = 9

∴ The initial number of women employed is 9.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 

In the first case:

N women can complete the project in 12 days.

In the second case:

If 5 women are less employed then it will take 15 more days to complete the same project.

**Formula used:**

M1D1 = M2D2 

Where, 

In the first case:

The number of women employed = M1 

The time is taken to complete the work = D₁ days

In the second case:

The number of women employed = M2

The time is taken to complete the work = D2 days

**Calculation:**

In the first case:

The number of women employed, M₁ = N

The time is taken to complete the work, D₁ = 12 days

In the second case:

The number of women employed, M2 = N - 5

The time is taken to complete the work, D2 = 12 + 15 = 27 days

Now, 

⇒ M₁D₁ = M2D2 

⇒ (N × 12) = (N - 5) × 27

⇒ 12N = 27N - 135

⇒ 15N = 135

⇒ N = 9

**∴ The initial number of women employed is 9.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] __Additional Information__**

questions.question: If March 27, 2011 was Sunday, what was the day on June 27, 2012?
questions.solution:
27th March 2011 = Sunday

Total Days between 27th March 2011 to 27th June 2012 is 1 years and 3 months.

2011 = Normal Year,

2012 = Leap Year,

Leap year = (52 weeks + 2 Odd days).

Non-leap year = (52 weeks + 1 Odd days).

So, 2011 = 1 odd days,

2012 = 2 odd days (leap year),

March (4 days left) = 4 odd days

April (full month) = 2 odd days

May (full month) = 3 odd days

June (till 27) = 6 odd days

Now total odd days = 2 (Leap year) + 4 + 2 + 3 + 6 = 17 i.e. 3 odd day.

So, Sunday + 3 = .Wednesday

27th June 2012 = Wednesday

Hence, the correct answer is "Wednesday".

__Basic Structure of a Calendar:-__

1. Ordinary year: Any year which 365 days is called an ordinary year. Ex: 1879, 2009, 2019, etc.

2. Leap year: Any year which has 366 days is called a leap year. Ex: 2012, 2016, 2020 etc.

3. The division of the number 365 by 7 gives the quotient 52 and remainder 1 which indicates that an ordinary year has 52 weeks and one extra day. This extra day is referred to as an “odd day” throughout the calendar topics.

4. A leap year has 366 days, the division of the number 366 by 7 gives the quotient 52 and remainder 2. This indicates that a leap year has 52 weeks and 2 extra days. These two extra days are also referred to as “odd days”.

5. An ordinary year has one odd day, whereas a leap year has two odd days

questions.question: A 729 ml of a mixture contains milk and water in the ratio of 7 : 2. How much more water is to be added to get a new mixture containing milk and water in the ratio of 7 : 3?
questions.solution:
**Concept Used:**

The ratio is the relation among two or more numbers, which tells how much one number is bigger than the others. 

To solve the questions based on ratio, we use to assume a variable for the shared part among quantities.

**Calculation:**

Let the amount of milk is 7x while the amount of water is 2x in the mixture. Now, we have a total of 729 mL of the mixture. Thus,

⇒ 7x + 2x = 729 

⇒ 9x = 729

⇒ x = 729/9

⇒ x = 81 

Thus, the amount of milk

⇒ 7x = 7 × 81

⇒ 7x = 567 mL 

Amount of water

⇒ 2x = 2 × 81

⇒ 2x = 162 mL

Now, the new mixture has a ratio of 7:3.

For this, the amount of milk will be 7x and the amount of water is 3x.

Here, the quantity of milk is the same while the quantity of water is increasing. This increased quantity is,

⇒ 3x − 2x = x

⇒ 3x − 2x = 81 mL

So, a total of 81 mL water needs to be added to get a new mixture containing milk and water in the ratio of 7 : 3.

**Hence, the correct option is 1.**

questions.question: A train cross a pole in 25sec & it takes 40sec to cross a tunnel of length 300m find the speed of the train & length of train?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Extra time taken to cross the tunnel = 40 − 25 = 15 sec.

This extra 15 sec is exactly the time taken to cover the length of the 300 m tunnel.

Speed of the train = Extra distance ÷ Extra time = 300 ÷ 15 = 20 m/s.

Length of train = Speed × Time taken to cross the pole = 20 × 25 = 500 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 20 m/s , 500 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 Train (L)
 
• 
 
 Pole
 Time = 25 sec
 Dist = L
 
 
• 

 Case 2: Crossing a Tunnel
 
 Train (L)
 
 Tunnel (300 m)
 
 Time = 40 sec
 Dist = L + 300

**Given:**

Time to cross a pole = 25 sec

Time to cross a 300 m tunnel = 40 sec

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

**Calculation:**

Let the speed of the train be S and the length of the train be L.

⇒ In Case 1 (crossing a pole): Total distance covered is the length of the train.

⇒ S = L ÷ 25 ... (Equation 1)

⇒ In Case 2 (crossing a tunnel): Total distance covered is the length of the train plus the length of the tunnel.

⇒ S = (L + 300) ÷ 40 ... (Equation 2)

Since the speed of the train remains constant in both cases, equate Equation 1 and Equation 2:

⇒ L ÷ 25 = (L + 300) ÷ 40

⇒ 40 × L = 25 × (L + 300)

⇒ 40 × L = 25 × L + 7500

⇒ 40 × L − 25 × L = 7500

⇒ 15 × L = 7500

⇒ L = 500 m

Now, substitute the value of L back into Equation 1 to find the speed:

⇒ S = 500 ÷ 25

⇒ S = 20 m/s

**∴ The correct answer is 20 m/s , 500 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Crossing a Point Object

When a train passes a pole, a standing man, or a tree, the total distance traveled is strictly equal to the length of the train (D = L).

Crossing a Lengthy Object

When a train passes a platform, a bridge, or a tunnel, the total distance traveled is the length of the train plus the length of the object (D = Lₜᵣₐᵢₙ + Lₒbjₑ꜀ₜ).

Relative Speed Concept

If two trains are moving in opposite directions, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (S₁ + S₂). If they are moving in the same direction, the relative speed is the difference (S₁ − S₂).

questions.question: Seats for Mathematics, Physics and Biology in a school are in the ratio 5 : 7 : 8. There is a proposal to increase these seats by 40%, 50% and 75% respectively. What will be the ratio of increased seats?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Seats for Mathematics, Physics, and Biology are in the ratio 5:7:8.

Proposed increase:

Mathematics by 40%

Physics by 50%

Biology by 75%

**Calculation:**

Let the initial number of seats be:

⇒ Mathematics = 5x

⇒ Physics = 7x

⇒ Biology = 8x

After the proposed increase:

⇒ New Mathematics seats = 5x + 40% of 5x

⇒ New Mathematics seats = 5x + 2x = 7x

⇒ New Physics seats = 7x + 50% of 7x

⇒ New Physics seats = 7x + 3.5x = 10.5x

⇒ New Biology seats = 8x + 75% of 8x

⇒ New Biology seats = 8x + 6x = 14x

The new ratio is:

⇒ 7x : 10.5x : 14x

To simplify, we divide each term by the common factor 3.5x:

⇒ (7x / 3.5x) : (10.5x / 3.5x) : (14x / 3.5x)

⇒ 2 : 3 : 4

**∴ The ratio of increased seats is 2:3:4.**

questions.question: The present age of a teacher is 1(1)/(2) times the sum of the present ages of his two students. Six years hence, the ratio of his age to the sum of the ages of both the students will be 6 : 5. The present age of the teacher is:

The present age of a teacher is 1¹/₂ times the sum of the present ages of his two students.

Let the sum of the present ages of the two students be x years.

Sum of students' ages = x + 12

⇒ 5((3/2)x + 6) = 6(x + 12)

⇒ 5(3x/2 + 6) = 6x + 72

⇒ (15x/2 + 30) = 6x + 72

⇒ 15x + 60 = 12x + 144

⇒ 3x = 84

⇒ x = 28

Therefore, the present age of the teacher = (3/2) × 28 = 42 years

**∴ The correct answer is option (1).**

questions.question: Fundamental duties were not placed in Part III of the Indian Constitution because Part III is ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Justiciable**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Fundamental Duties of Indian citizens were **not part of the original Constitution**. These were introduced later by the **42nd Amendment Act in 1976**, based on the recommendations of the** Swaran Singh Committee**. The duties are listed in **Part IVA (Article 51A)** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Fundamental Duties, as per the Indian Constitution, have been established to promote a sense of respect and responsibility amongst citizens. Importantly, these **duties are non-justiciable**—they cannot be enforced through legal proceedings. This is in stark contrast with Fundamental Rights, which are enforceable in nature.
 
• The Fundamental Duties covered under **Article 51A are ten in number** and they were later expanded to **eleven by the 86th Amendment in 2002.**
 
• The Fundamental Rights, outlined in Part III of the constitution from **Article 12 to 35**, are integral to the Indian Constitution. Drafted by Dr. Ambedkar and the other framers of the Constitution, these rights were derived from the **US Bill of Rights, the Irish Constitution, and various other sources**. These rights are justiciable, meaning they can be enforced through the courts. If a person feels their Fundamental Rights have been violated, they can directly approach the Supreme Court or High Courts for enforcement or protection of such rights, according to **Article 32 and Article 226** of the Constitution respectively.
 
• Fundamental Duties were not included in this part to maintain a clear demarcation between the rights that are **enforceable by law (such as the fundamental rights) and moral obligations or responsibilities (such as the fundamental duties)** that are not legally enforceable.

questions.question: Average marks obtained by 19 boys of a college is 48. If the highest marks and lowest marks obtained are removed, then the average reduces by 4. What is the average of the highest and lowest marks obtained?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Average marks of 19 boys is 48. After removing highest and lowest marks, average of 17 boys is 44.

**Concept **

Average = Total Marks/Number of Students.

**Calculation:**

Total marks of 19 boys = 19 × 48 = 912

Total marks of 17 boys = 17 × 44 = 748

The sum of the highest and lowest marks = 912 - 748 = 164

The average of the highest and lowest marks = 164/2 = 82

**Hence, the average of the highest and lowest marks is 82.**
